title: Prospective clinical trial on the influence of biological age and systemic stress on the risk of perioperative cardiovascular complications in high-risk non-cardiac surgery
summary:
Following surgical procedures, approximately 20% of all patients suffer damage to the heart muscle. Such damage to the heart muscle has been linked to increased short- and long-term mortality. However, this heart muscle damage often occurs perioperatively without specific complaints or symptoms, and can only be detected by measuring heart-specific biomarkers such as hs-Troponin T. New biomarkers will therefore be needed in future that can be measured either before surgery or shortly after admission to the intensive care unit to assess the risk of such perioperative heart muscle damage. 

In this study, the above-mentioned cardiac marker hs-Troponin T is systematically measured before and after surgery in patients undergoing complex, high-risk non-cardiac surgery followed by a stay in an intensive care unit. This will enable us to investigate how many of the patients suffer heart muscle damage during the operation. In addition, various markers of biological age – which have not previously been investigated in routine hospital practice – as well as cardiovascular and stress biomarkers will be analysed from blood samples taken before and after surgery (see below for exact timings). 
These data will then be used to investigate whether any of the measured biomarkers – taken either before surgery or shortly after surgery – are suitable for predicting perioperative myocardial injury or death due to perioperative cardiovascular complications. This study will also investigate the influence of frailty on the likelihood of the above-mentioned cardiovascular complications occurring. Frailty is assessed prior to surgery using questionnaires and simple tests, such as handgrip strength measurement; biological age is also determined using a non-invasive skin test that measures the accumulation of certain ageing products (known as advanced glycation end-products). Cardiovascular complications and deaths are recorded in telephone follow-up interviews with patients after one, three and twelve months.

interventions.name: The study includes patients aged ≥ 45 years who undergo elective, non-cardiac high-risk surgery with planned postoperative admission on intensive care unit. This includes, in particular, complex visceral and thoracic surgical procedures (including liver, oesophageal, pancreatic and intestinal surger

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ability to give consent, planned post-operative admission to the anaesthesiology intensive care unit following elective, non-cardiac surgical procedures involving a high procedural risk
Exclusion criteria:
Cardiac surgery, emergency and urgent surgery (N0–N2), patients unable to give consent, age < 45 years, refusal to participate in the study, pregnancy, previous surgery within the last 2 weeks, acute infectious disease (gastroenteritis, cholecystitis, appendicitis, peritonitis, pneumonia, etc.) within the previous 2 weeks
